title: Jesse Crier sings 'Poor Little Me'
summary: Crier was a singer brought in for one number at the same session and had worked at the Saratoga Club.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Then there was another question of a vocalist. On that
same session, you did a number called "Poor Little Me," which was a Paul Barbarin number.
And there was a vocalist on that, and I remember you told me that it was Jesse Crier(?).
That's right. That's right. He was just a singer. That's all he ever did, was sing. He was a singer just to come in and do that one number with the band, you know. Yeah, Jesse Crier.
So he must have been there, then, when Razaf came in.
Well, I don't know if they were recorded the same day. Were they?
Yeah, it's listed as the same session.
You also did "Louisiana Swing" at that time.
But Jesse Crier would have been hired just for the one...

Well, he was performing... We worked together at the Saratoga Club for quite a while. And he worked at different theatres, the Lafayette Theatre, in Washington and Philadelphia. He was around to different clubs and things. He was very popular. He was a good singer, too. A very good singer.
Was he sort of a regular with the Russell band, then, at that time?

No. But we happened to work some spots together; I mean, at the same time, you know. He had nothing to do with us coming into the spots, and we had nothing to do with him coming and working in the spots. But I mean, we worked together on the spots.
